Incorporating SLOOS evidence into the December 2018 FOMC assessment:

- The FOMC statement highlights strong current conditions (solid job gains, low unemployment, robust household spending) with inflation near 2%, a 25 bp hike to 2.25–2.50%, and guidance for “some further gradual increases,” alongside continued balance-sheet runoff.
- The Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates banks tightened standards on C&I loans and on construction and land development loans, tightened other nonprice terms across firm sizes, and reported weaker demand for construction and land development loans. This points to more restrictive credit supply and cooling loan demand in risk-sensitive categories.
- These SLOOS signals corroborate the moderation in business fixed investment and imply an incremental headwind to capex and growth via tighter bank intermediation, effectively amplifying the tightening from rate hikes and balance-sheet runoff.
- Combined with financial stability considerations (elevated valuations, higher business leverage), the SLOOS tilt argues for a more cautious forward-looking tone than the statement alone, even as current activity remains strong.

Net take: Positive on current conditions but more clearly constrained by tightening bank credit and softer loan demand; forward-looking tone is modestly positive, with greater downside risk to growth/capex than previously assessed.
